Quick notes from network side:

- Pattern: VPC private endpoint (no IGW) -> NAT/FW is disallowed. We recommend an internal proxy appliance (HA pair) with outbound only to the approved HEC private IP. The proxy performs mTLS termination and forwards to Splunk HEC.
- Ports: outbound 8088 (HEC), 4317 (OTLP) for optional trace-forwarder -> both over mTLS.
- Sizing: for their expected token rate (see sheet), a pair of t3-equivalent collectors with 4 vCPU/16GB each should handle up to 10k events/sec with small batching. Add disk buffer (20GB) for short-term retention during transient connectivity.
- Evidence path: use an S3-compatible on-prem bucket behind their private endpoint for durable handoff if direct HEC is not allowed; Redwood will pull/push only via the approved endpoint when authorized.

Draft runbook notes (high level) — will paste into redwood_vpc_runbook_draft.md:

Overview
- Scope: Private VPC deployments (AtlasBank) — logs, metrics, traces. Assumes no internet egress.
- Goals: deterministic delivery to customer SIEM, preserve trace context, provide auditable evidence package.

Collector model
- Preferred: sidecar collector (OpenTelemetry Collector) for per-service tracing and metrics; use a daemonset for host-level logs (filebeat/fluentbit).
- Buffering: local disk spool for up to 72 hours by default. Configurable per-customer. Encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS or HSM integration.

Authentication
- mTLS between collectors and the HEC/proxy. Certificate provisioning via customer CA or Redwood-provided CSR flow. Automated cert rotation and cert revocation lists documented.

Tracing hooks
- Redwood runtime inserts lightweight tracehooks at request ingress/egress points. We preserve W3C Trace Context and B3 where present; OTLP exporters forward spans to the OTLP endpoint at 4317 if allowed.

Audit and evidence
- Audit logs: every export attempt, batching events, and ack receipts are logged and retained in the local audit store; push proofs (hashes + timestamps) to the customer's on-prem evidence bucket on successful handoff.

Action items for AtlasBank packet:
- Confirm HEC internal IP/CIDR and accepted client certificate CN pattern.
- Decide on customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed key for on-disk encryption.

Thanks for the requirements. Attached is our initial package for your compliance team: a concise runbook, a network diagram, and the requirements spreadsheet with inline mappings. Highlights:

- Collector pattern: sidecars + daemonset with local disk spool (configurable 24–120h).
- Network: internal proxy pattern — no IGW/Internet egress. mTLS to HEC on port 8088; OTLP optional to 4317.
- Tracing: W3C Trace Context preserved end-to-end; Redwood injects minimal tracehooks at gateway and service runtime.
